summary: The admitted v68 burial replay stops when a buried organic sack's ROT_ORGANIC timer becomes due. The JavaScript timeout table has no callback for rot_organic(), and the existing js/dig.js function only performs the corpse-safe extraction path; it omits C's loop that transfers and buries every container child at the container's buried coordinates before freeing the container.

mismatch.message: elapsed-turn nh_timeout requires a ported timeout function, but rot_organic() is due

source.branch: dig.c:rot_organic() receives the due ROT_ORGANIC callback for a buried organic container. Before extracting and freeing the container, C repeatedly copies its ox/oy to the first child and calls bury_an_obj(child); this removes each child from the container, buries it at the same coordinates, and can schedule that child's own ROT_ORGANIC timer. JS has only the corpse contents-free extraction path registered in dig.js, while timeout.js leaves the ROT_ORGANIC table slot without a function.
callers: dig.c:bury_an_obj() schedules ROT_ORGANIC when an eligible organic object is buried; the admitted recipe places a metal dagger in an organic sack, buries the sack, lets its timer expire, and later digs up the child's surviving buried object.
timeout.c:run_timers() invokes timeout_funcs[ROT_ORGANIC].f() for the due timer; js/timeout.js:run_timers() dispatches the matching timeout_funcs entry, which currently has no f for rot_organic.
dependencies: dig.c:bury_an_obj() (already implemented in js/bury.js and used to transfer each child)

evidence: The accepted v68 evaluation records 372/554 screens, 3870/4153 RNG calls, and 372/554 cursors before the replay stops at step 372 with the due rot_organic() timeout refusal. The saved queue identifies manifest challenges/manifests/v68.json (SHA-256 f24f70ec92301004f8c070fdf94a3a2d318a19231ca193ce52e888320beaaa3e), recording challenges/cases/v68/v68-buried-filled-sack-action8.session.json (SHA-256 2aaed7f2acc8fc014f26e8db273ce4052c3f1dc6cfc045bdc8ac276c74846069), and evaluation challenges/evaluations/admission-f5371e6adf39dfbf6b3bc839f5d6d96195f0536f-v68.json from commit f5371e6adf39dfbf6b3bc839f5d6d96195f0536f.

The C recipe's independent observation records a dagger inside an organic sack buried with #wizbury; C schedules the sack's ROT_ORGANIC timer, then on expiry transfers the dagger into the buried-object list at the sack coordinates and frees the sack. Later digging reveals the dagger without the sack. The recipe is challenges/cases/v68/v68-buried-filled-sack-action8.recipe.session.json; its comments retain the actual C queue, timer, and terrain observations.

Upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/dig.c:2125-2140 implements rot_organic(): while Has_contents(obj), set the first child's ox/oy to the container coordinates and call bury_an_obj(child), then obj_extract_self(obj) and obfree(obj, NULL). The child call's return is discarded. The existing js/dig.js:2449-2455 implements only extraction and obfree, with a comment explicitly leaving the buried-container contents loop unported.

Upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/timeout.c:2216-2240 dispatches the callback selected by timeout_funcs. js/timeout.js:600-610 has a ROT_ORGANIC row with no f; js/timeout.js:2295-2310 refuses the due timer before dispatch when that row lacks a handler. The implementation scope is the complete dig.c:rot_organic() behavior plus its timeout-table wiring, retaining child coordinate updates, recursive bury_an_obj() effects and random calls, and final container disposal in C order.
